title: fix(plugin-form,components): master-detail edit lines and element:record_picker options re-read on the data-invalidation bus (objectui#10853)
body:
Fixes #10853
Clause-②: no — two readers subscribe to the existing invalidation bus; no declared key, export or accept set moves.

This is the fifth batch of bus readers under decision B on objectui#10519 ("readers first"). After PR objectui#10777 removes `PageView`'s remount, these two blocks would otherwise keep showing data from before a page action. objectui#10519 remains open.

Dispatched by the `domain:ui` seat 4 PM (claim comment 5860833997, triage 5860720827). Session: `https://claude.ai/code/session_01MCg3z5cGrV51xEddpGcxEY`. In `mode:subagent` that id is also this run's. Branch `claude/issue-10853-master-detail-picker-bus-readers` was cut from `origin/main` `a7fd877` (BASE). Head is `a13048c`, after one patch round on the contract review of `ac526b1` (see **Patch round** below).

## What changed

Each read now takes a nonce from the data-invalidation bus for the object it queries. This follows the objectui#10623 / objectui#10778 shape: the same bus, the same matcher (`dataChangeMatches`), no second channel and no remount.

- **`packages/plugin-form/src/MasterDetailForm.tsx`, edit mode.** Each detail collection's `find` of its child object now re-reads when the bus reports a change to that child object, or `'*'`. The re-read happens in place, and the rows and the save baseline move together.
  - The collections are authored, so their number is not fixed, and one `useDataInvalidation` call per object cannot be made. A local `useObjectsInvalidation(names)` subscribes through `subscribeDataChanges`, the listener set `useDataInvalidation` itself uses. It tests each change with `dataChangeMatches` at object level and keys on the set's content.
  - Nothing new is exported. The claim's `Clause-②: no` holds.
  - The load now runs one collection at a time: a per-collection read number, plus a generation the load effect's teardown bumps. So the load on mount, a record change, a bus re-read and a replay each commit only if they are that collection's latest read.
  - A collection only re-reads for its own child object. The header re-reads through its own `ObjectForm` (objectui#10572), which is unchanged.
  - The row editor ("Open row") holds its collection's re-read while it is open (patch round).
- **`packages/components/src/renderers/basic/record-picker.tsx`.** The option read's effect now names `useDataInvalidation(object)`, subscribed only when the adapter reads and the object has resolved. A read of exactly the query whose options are already on screen (same adapter, object, filter, sort and limit) runs in place:
  - there is no `setLoading(true)`, so the control stays enabled and shows no "Loading…";
  - the answer swaps the options when it lands and clears an earlier failure;
  - the bound page variable is never written.

  Any other read starts from "Loading…", as before. The `placeholder` input's description now says so ("while it reads a new set of options"). That is a text change only; the input's `type` is unchanged.
- **`object-form` with `subforms`** routes to the same `MasterDetailForm`, so the same reader covers it. This is pinned. The spec refuses `subforms` on `object-form`, so this does not gate (triage note 5).
- **`.changeset/10853-master-detail-picker-bus-readers.md`:** `@object-ui/plugin-form` patch and `@object-ui/components` patch.
- **`.changeset/10778-dashboard-bus-readers.md`:** one appended dated note in the objectui#10533 form (triage note 4). It says the `drillDown.report` drawer does re-read since objectui#10814 (PR objectui#10836), and points at `drillDownReport.invalidationRefetch-10814.test.tsx`. The single-record drawer half of that sentence still holds. The frontmatter is byte-identical: md5 of lines 1-3 is `d527064c725ab089f1c5e8f4c419e8cd` before and after, and `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` reports the declared bump unchanged (`@object-ui/plugin-dashboard: patch`).

## Unsaved lines (B3): held, then replayed after a save or a revert

This is the objectui#10712 R3 / objectui#10572 rule, applied to each collection separately.

- **Unsaved** means the edit save's row diff (`buildMasterDetailEditBatch`) finds something to write to that collection other than the parent link. A user's edit therefore reads as unsaved exactly when the save would send it, and a line changed back to its stored value reads as saved again.
  - The parent link is set aside on purpose, and it is the one place the two disagree. The save restates the link on every row it writes, as the parent id in string form. Against a backend that returns the link as a number or an expanded lookup, the save restates it on every row while the lines read as saved. That restatement is not user input, so it does not hold a re-read. `sendBatch` is unchanged.
- **An open row editor counts as unsaved** for its collection (patch round). The editor keeps its draft in its own form, not in the rows, so the rows alone cannot show it.
- **A held bus re-read** is replayed once, when the row editor is closed (Apply or Close) and either:
  - **revert:** the collection's lines read as saved again; or
  - **save:** this form's save has landed. `sendBatch` marks every collection the batch wrote, and the replay runs once the save guard releases.

  After Apply the applied line is unsaved, so the re-read stays held until that line is saved or changed back.
- **A line typed while a re-read is in flight is kept, in the grid or in the row editor.**
  - The answer only commits over the same rows the read was issued over, and never while the row editor is open on that collection. That check sits both before and inside the `setRowState` updater.
  - Otherwise the re-read is held behind the edit.
  - Unlike `LineItemsPanel`, the grid is not disabled during a re-read, and the row editor is never reset, re-keyed or disabled by one. Only a save disables it, as before.
- **A failed re-read keeps the lines on screen** and warns. A failed load still leaves the collection empty, as before.
  - A bus event during the FIRST load supersedes that load. If that re-read then fails, the warning now says "no lines have been read for it yet" instead of "the lines on screen are kept" (patch round, a one-line change).

## The picker's bound value (B4)

- A re-read never writes the page variable.
- If the bound record is no longer among the re-read options, the variable keeps its value and the trigger shows no label. It shows neither the old label nor the placeholder: Radix draws the placeholder only for an empty value, and no offered item carries the value. This is the same thing the picker has always shown for a value outside its options, for example one beyond `limit`.
- When a later read offers that record again, its label returns.

All of this is pinned.

## Patch round (contract review of `ac526b1`: FAIL)

The review (comment 5861421338) found one defect, and it is verified: with the row editor open on a line, a bus event committed fresh row copies under it. `expandedRow` then changed, and the editor's inline `initialData` reset overwrote the draft.

- Measured at `ac526b1` with the new pins: the draft read `'first (server)'` where the user had typed `'first (draft)'`.
- When the server dropped the line, the editor was reset to its neighbour (`'second'`), so a later Apply would have mapped onto that row.

What changed in the fix:

- `MasterDetailForm.tsx`: the `expanded` state moves above the lines reader. A render-time `rowEditorEntryRef` (the same pattern as `rowStateRef`) names the collection the editor is open on, and three places read it:
  - the hold decision counts that collection as unsaved;
  - both in-flight commit sites hold instead of committing while it is open;
  - the replay effect skips it while it is open and runs again when `expanded` changes.
- The failed re-read warning is now accurate for a collection that never loaded.
- `linesUnsaved`'s doc, the changeset and this body now claim only what holds about the parent link.
- The changeset sentence about a line typed in flight now names both the grid and the row editor, and says an open editor is never reset by a re-read.
- **Two pending changesets re-read** against this diff, per the changeset-claim-re-read bot. Both hold, and neither is edited:
  - `.changeset/6726-find-envelope-records-arms.md`: its row "`element:record_picker` options" still describes the picker, whose read is still `res?.data ?? (Array.isArray(res) ? res : [])`. A `{ records }` answer still reads as no rows, on a first read and on a re-read.
  - `.changeset/6783-readprops-degenerate-config-bag.md`: the picker still reads its bag through `readProps`, which this diff does not touch.

## Mechanism assumptions, measured

- **B1 (templates).** I read both merged diffs.
  - PR objectui#10836: `LineItemsPanel` holds edits and keeps the grid drawn with `refreshing`.
  - PR objectui#10837: `DatasetWidget` / `DashboardRenderer`, one reader per widget component.

  I reused the seam. The picker needed the in-place path because its re-read flipped `loading`. The master-detail lines needed no refreshing state: at BASE their edit-mode read had no loading branch, so a re-read never blanked them.
- **B2 (sites re-read 0 times at BASE).** Confirmed with an uncommitted scratch probe on BASE `a7fd877`: the real `SchemaRenderer`, real registrations, one `notifyDataChanged({ objectName: '*' })`, and a bare `useDataInvalidation` reader as the lit control. Results, counted as reads on mount → reads after the event:

  | site | before → after |
  |:--|:--|
  | detail lines (`find` of `po_line`) | `2 → 2` |
  | header (`findOne`) | `1 → 2` |
  | picker options | `1 → 1` |
  | control nonce | `1` |

  Mount reads the lines twice because the load effect runs again once the resolved details are set. That is unchanged, and the pins count from rest.
- **B3 / B4.** See the two sections above.

## Pins and ablation

- **The pins.** `MasterDetailForm.busReread-10853.test.tsx` (12 tests: 8, plus 4 for the row editor) and `record-picker.busReread-10853.test.tsx` (4 tests) render through the real `SchemaRenderer` and the packages' own registrations. The master-detail pins use the real line-item grid; the picker pins sit in a real `PageVariablesProvider` with a variable bound to the picker. A bare `useDataInvalidation` reader is the lit control, and reads can be held open to look at the block mid-flight.
- **What they cover.**
  - `'*'` re-reads once in place: the same input node, no blanking. A save afterwards writes no line, so the baseline moved.
  - A child-object event re-reads; an unrelated object does not.
  - Two collections each answer only to their own object.
  - Held then revert; held then save (exactly one replay each).
  - A line typed in flight is kept.
  - Row editor, through the real form ("Open row", type into its fields):
    - a bus event rewrites the line: the draft is intact, Apply writes that line, the save sends `update l1 { label, memo }`, and the held re-read replays once after the save;
    - the server drops the line: the draft is intact, and Apply and the save target `l1`, not its neighbour;
    - Close without Apply replays the held re-read once;
    - a re-read already in flight when the editor opens does not commit under it, and replays once on close.
  - The `subforms` route re-reads.
  - Picker: in place with the value kept; its own object versus an unrelated one; the bound record gone and then back.
  - Controls: create mode and a picker with no object read nothing.

Restored: blob == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` 0 bytes |

Two ablation attempts in the patch round, reported as they happened:

- **The first A5 attempt, at `ea52c79`, crashed the worker (`Worker exited unexpectedly`) instead of failing.** At that head the commit guard held by re-asking, and with the hold decision ablated the re-ask looped. The shipped code cannot loop, because both checks read the same ref, but `a13048c` makes the guard hold directly so the two checks no longer depend on each other. A5 was then re-run cleanly (above).
- **Ablating only the outer commit site stayed green** (`Tests 12 passed`): the updater site alone covers it. That is why A6 mutates both sites.

No `dist/` preflight applies: each pin imports its package's registration through a relative source path, and both mutated files are reached through it.

## Serial

- `git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD` at `a13048c` against a fresh `origin/main` (`e32dae1`, fetched into a private ref, since deleted): clean. No commit on main since BASE touches these three files.
- `PageView` is not touched (PR objectui#10777, seat 2).

## Acceptance notes

Not changed here. Each was read at source unless it says it was measured.

- The lines subscribe to each collection's child object only. A write declared on the PARENT object, for example a record action that rewrites lines on the server and announces the parent, re-reads the header but not the lines. `'*'`, which `PageView` will send, does both. This is the same boundary `LineItemsPanel` has.
- Measured at BASE and unchanged: the edit-mode lines are read twice on mount. The load effect runs again when the resolved details are first set, even when nothing needed resolving, and the first read is superseded. Carrier: none.
- Unchanged: a failed first load of a collection's lines still leaves it empty with no message. Only the new re-read path keeps the lines and warns. Carrier: none.
- The picker's in-place re-read that fails shows "Failed to load" and disables the control, the same as a failed first load. The options it had stay in state and come back with the next read that lands.
- With the console's mutation bridge mounted, the save's own batch echoes on the bus while its collections still read unsaved. By the ordering read at source, that echo is held and replayed once after the save, so there is one extra read per written collection, in place. The pins' adapter has no `onMutation`, so this is not pinned.
- `element:record_picker`'s `emptyText` input description cites a line address, `:213` read at `a7fd877`, for the "No records" default. At `a7fd877` that line is inside a comment block, not the default. This is a stale same-file line address in published registry text, outside this card's class, so it is not repaired here. Carrier: none.
